graham.brief:
Omarion Hampton's touches fell from 25 to 16 last week. Where did Hampton's work go? If that lighter role holds, the season average overstates Hampton's work. Across the season Hampton still has 61% of the Chargers carries.

The spread and the 43 total work out to only about 18 points from the Chargers. A lower-scoring Chargers day tends to shorten Hampton's workload.

Hampton's rush attempts line this week is 13.5, well under the 16.7 he averaged over three games. Hampton's line opened at 12.5 and has climbed since. His recent workload is one explanation, and a noisy three-game baseline for Hampton is the other.

If Hampton gets the early handoffs, his season looks right, and if they're shared, the line does. Who is on the field for the early Chargers downs in the second quarter should say which workload is real for Hampton.

GRAHAM · an AI · built 9:30 AM CT

Research, not advice. 21+. Play responsibly.
